older_added_or_changed_fields.summary: Moses’ older brother and spokesman, appointed with his sons to the priestly office. While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes the golden calf and proclaims a feast, making him central to that breach of worship. Like Moses he is barred from entering Canaan after Meribah; his priestly garments pass to Eleazar before he dies on Mount Hor.

Shaphat’s son from Abel-meholah, called from plowing to follow Elijah and recognized as his successor after taking up his mantle. His stories include provision for a widow, restoring a child to life, Naaman’s healing, and a curse followed by bears mauling forty-two mockers. He also intervenes in royal affairs and sends a prophet to anoint Jehu.

A man from the land of Uz, described as upright and fearing God. He loses his children, possessions, and health, disputes his friends’ explanations of his suffering, and addresses God. After God answers him, Job prays for his friends and the closing account describes the restoration of his fortunes and family.

Joshua, also called Jeshua, was the son of Jozadak and high priest of the returned community. He worked with Zerubbabel to restore worship and rebuild the temple.

Nun’s son from Ephraim, also called Oshea and Jehoshua, who serves Moses and is commissioned as his successor. He leads Israel across the Jordan and in the conquest narratives, including Jericho’s capture and the killing of its inhabitants. His leadership also concerns dividing the land and renewing the covenant at Shechem, where he calls the people to choose whom they will serve.

geography.origin: An Ephraimite; birthplace not specified in the cited passages (Numbers 13:8)

Philip was one of the twelve apostles. John recounts his call, his invitation to Nathanael to meet Jesus, and his request to be shown the Father.
Philip is identified as the brother of Herod and the husband of Herodias before she married Herod. He is distinct from Philip the apostle and Philip the tetrarch.
Philip was tetrarch of Ituraea and the region of Trachonitis when John the Baptist began his ministry. Luke identifies him as a brother of Herod the tetrarch.
Philip was one of the seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem believers. He preached in Samaria and explained Isaiah to the Ethiopian eunuch; Acts later calls him the evangelist.

Zimmah is named in 2 Chronicles 29:12. KJV context: “Then the Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites: and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehalelel: and of the Gershonites; Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah:”
Zimran is named in Genesis 25:2. KJV context: “And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.”

Zimri is named in Numbers 25:14. KJV context: “Now the name of the Israelite that was slain, even that was slain with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites.”

Zimri is named in 1 Kings 16:9. KJV context: “And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.”
Zimri is named in 1 Chronicles 8:36. KJV context: “And Ahaz begat Jehoadah; and Jehoadah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza,”
Ziph is named in 1 Samuel 26:2. KJV context: “Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.”
Ziphah is named in 1 Chronicles 4:16. KJV context: “And the sons of Jehaleleel; Ziph, and Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel.”
Zippor is named in Numbers 22:2. KJV context: “And Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.”
Zipporah was the daughter of the priest of Midian and the wife of Moses. Exodus names her sons Gershom and Eliezer and recounts her action during the journey to Egypt.
Zithri is named in Exodus 6:22. KJV context: “And the sons of Uzziel; Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Zithri.”
Ziza is named in 1 Chronicles 4:37. KJV context: “And Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah;”
Ziza is named in 2 Chronicles 11:20. KJV context: “And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.”
Zizah is named in 1 Chronicles 23:10. KJV context: “And the sons of Shimei were, Jahath, Zina, and Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.”
Zobebah is named in 1 Chronicles 4:8. KJV context: “And Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.”

Zohar is named in Genesis 23:8. KJV context: “And he communed with them, saying, If it be your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight; hear me, and intreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,”
Zoheth is named in 1 Chronicles 4:20. KJV context: “And the sons of Shimon were, Amnon, and Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. And the sons of Ishi were, Zoheth, and Benzoheth.”
Zophah is named in 1 Chronicles 7:35. KJV context: “And the sons of his brother Helem; Zophah, and Imna, and Shelesh, and Amal.”
Zophar the Naamathite was one of the three friends who came to comfort Job. His speeches appear in Job 11 and 20; the closing chapter includes him among those directed to offer sacrifice.
Zorobabel is named in Luke 3:27. KJV context: “Which was the son of Joanna, which was the son of Rhesa, which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri,”
Zuar is named in Numbers 1:8. KJV context: “Of Issachar; Nethaneel the son of Zuar.”

Zuph is named in 1 Samuel 1:1. KJV context: “Now there was a certain man of Ramathaimzophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite:”
Zur is named in Numbers 25:15. KJV context: “And the name of the Midianitish woman that was slain was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur; he was head over a people, and of a chief house in Midian.”

Zur is named in Numbers 31:8. KJV context: “And they slew the kings of Midian, beside the rest of them that were slain; namely, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.”
Zur is named in 1 Chronicles 8:30. KJV context: “And his firstborn son Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Nadab,”

Zuriel is named in Numbers 3:35. KJV context: “And the chief of the house of the father of the families of Merari was Zuriel the son of Abihail: these shall pitch on the side of the tabernacle northward.”
Zurishaddai is named in Numbers 1:6. KJV context: “Of Simeon; Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.”
